tasks.configuration: Scope: two large food processing plants propose to locate in the service area, adding high strength flow in large batches.

cards.label: Confirm the treatment interface can accept the load pattern and record any conditions the plant operator sets
Agree discharge conditions, including equalization or release timing the plants must provide to protect the system
Characterize the proposed discharges with the proponents, including peak batch volumes, timing, and strength in general terms
Price any system work the discharges require under the funding policy and record the agreement before approval
Check hydraulic capacity for the batch peaks at every element, since average flow alone understates the impact
Set monitoring at the connections so actual discharge patterns are checked against the agreement from the first month

tasks.explanation: Batch discharges break plans built on averages, so peaks and timing lead the assessment. Connection monitoring from the first month is what makes the agreement real.

tasks.configuration: Scope: the fleet has grown by accretion, with many pump models, control types, and spare parts that do not interchange.

cards.label: Apply the standards to renewals and new stations first, rather than replacing serviceable equipment only for uniformity
Track standardization progress as stations renew, and report fleet variety reduction in the annual asset review
Inventory the fleet by pump model, control type, age, and condition, and find where variety creates cost or delay
Review the standards every five years against performance and supplier support so they do not freeze outdated choices
Define standard station classes by size and duty, with preferred pumps, controls, and fittings for each class
Set the spare parts holding from the standard classes so critical spares are stocked once and shared across stations

tasks.explanation: Standardization pays through spares, training, and faster repairs, not through uniformity itself. Applying it at renewal avoids scrapping good equipment to meet a tidiness goal.

tasks.prompt: Order the lift station renewal prioritization across the fleet.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: renewal funding covers about four stations a year, and candidates include the oldest, the least reliable, and the highest consequence stations.

cards.label: Sequence the program so design for next year stations starts while this year construction runs
Build the candidate list from condition, failure history, run hours, and the consequence of an outage at each station
Report the stations deferred each year with their risk, so the board sees what the funding level leaves exposed
Score the candidates on likelihood and consequence together, so a small unreliable station does not outrank a critical fragile one
Fund emergency replacements from a stated contingency rather than by displacing the planned program silently
Inspect the top candidates to confirm condition firsthand, including wet well structure, pumps, controls, and standby power

tasks.explanation: Likelihood and consequence together prevent both age only and size only rankings. A stated contingency keeps one failure from quietly consuming the whole renewal program.

tasks.prompt: Order a standby power strategy for the lift station fleet.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: a regional outage caused two station overflows last year, and standby coverage varies from fixed generators to none.

cards.label: Confirm the actual time to overflow by records or test for the highest consequence stations, not by design assumption
Test the full response in an exercise that includes a night outage scenario at a high consequence station
Close the gaps in priority order, including transfer switches, fuel storage, and exercise routines for fixed units
Classify stations by overflow consequence during an outage, including time to overflow from wet well and storage in the sewers
Set the coverage standard per class, from fixed generation to portable generator connection points to response only
Create the portable generator deployment plan with towing, connection, and staffing worked out before the next outage

tasks.explanation: Time to overflow is the number the whole strategy hangs on, so it is verified, not assumed. An exercised deployment plan matters because portable generation fails on logistics more than on equipment.

tasks.prompt: Order a fleet energy management program for lift stations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: energy is a major operating cost, stations vary widely in energy per cubic metre pumped, and no one owns the variance.

cards.label: Set an energy measure per station class and report it in the fleet review with the actions taken
Correct the operational causes first, including level settings, pump sequencing, and ragging that forces inefficient running
Rank stations by energy per cubic metre and investigate the worst performers for wear, throttling, and oversized operation
Build the business case for equipment changes only where measured waste exceeds the cost of correction with given rates
Meter or estimate energy and pumped volume per station on one basis so stations can be compared fairly
Re rank annually so improvement is tracked and new poor performers are caught early

tasks.explanation: Fair comparison needs one measurement basis, because raw energy bills punish large stations unfairly. Operational causes come before capital because level settings and ragging waste more energy than motor age in most fleets.

tasks.prompt: Order the wet well operating strategy review across the fleet.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: grease and solids problems differ by station, some wells cycle pumps excessively, and level settings were set station by station without a standard.

cards.label: Review problem stations after one season and extend what worked to similar stations in the fleet
Set level bands by station class that balance pump starts, storage use, and solids settling time in the well
Standardize the settings in the control documentation so future changes follow the management of change process
Adjust the worst stations first and record the before and after starts, cleaning need, and odour reports
Add mixing or cleaning actions where level changes alone cannot control grease and sediment
Review each problem station record, including starts per hour, grease findings, odour complaints, and pump ragging history

tasks.explanation: Level settings trade pump wear against well cleanliness, so they are set by class with evidence. Recording before and after results is what turns adjustments into a fleet standard.

tasks.prompt: Order a force main asset strategy for the fleet.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: the utility operates 40 force mains, several are old, air management is inconsistent, and a recent break flooded a roadway.

cards.label: Build the force main register with age, material, length, pressure duty, and break history for every main
Assess surge protection where pump trips can damage old pipe, and correct the worst exposures first
Set break response readiness per high risk main, including isolation points, bypass routes, and repair fittings stocked
Rank mains by break consequence and condition evidence, including surge exposure and air valve state
Plan renewal or lining for the mains whose condition and consequence justify it, phased with station renewals
Inspect air release and vacuum valves on the highest risk mains and restore the maintenance cycle for all of them

tasks.explanation: Air valves are small assets whose neglect breaks large pipes, so their cycle is restored early. Break readiness per main shortens the worst day, which for a force main is measured in flooding and road closure.

tasks.prompt: Order the alarm and telemetry strategy for the lift station fleet.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: alarm quality varies, one station alarms so often that staff discount it, and a real high level event was missed elsewhere.

cards.label: Set alarm priorities and escalation, including who is called when the first call is not acknowledged in a stated time
Review alarm performance quarterly and treat repeat nuisance alarms as defects to fix, not background noise
Rationalize alarm lists so each alarm means a defined condition needing a defined response, and remove nuisance alarms at their cause
Train responders on the revised alarm set and record the training before the new lists go live
Audit alarm history per station, counting alarms, response times, and how many required any action
Confirm communications backup for high consequence stations so a telemetry failure itself alarms

tasks.explanation: An alarm that usually means nothing trains staff to ignore the one that matters. Escalation on non acknowledgement closes the gap that a missed night alarm exposes.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to chronic pump ragging at several stations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: wipes and fibrous material clog pumps weekly at six stations, pulling crews from planned work and raising overflow risk.

cards.label: Track unclogging calls per station monthly and keep the fix open until the rate falls and stays down
Confirm the pattern from work records, including which stations, which pumps, and what material is removed each time
Run a public source message in the worst catchments about wipes, coordinated with the cleaning program findings
Share the results across the fleet review so similar stations are corrected before they reach the same state
Apply the fix per station, from pump or impeller change to level and sequencing changes that keep material moving
Check station hydraulics for causes, including impeller type, low velocity periods, and wet well dead zones where material collects

tasks.explanation: Ragging is treated per station because the same symptom has different causes. Tracking the call rate until it stays down prevents declaring victory after one quiet month.

tasks.prompt: Order a lift station decommissioning where a gravity diversion replaces it.

tasks.configuration: Scope: a new gravity trunk lets one old station be retired, removing its energy, maintenance, and overflow risk permanently.

cards.label: Transfer flows in stages with the station kept ready to restart until the new route has passed a significant storm
Update the asset register, alarm lists, and emergency plans so no response still routes crews to the retired station
Remove pumps, controls, and hazardous materials, and make the wet well safe by filling or conversion as designed
Prove the gravity route carries the full station catchment at peak wet weather flow before any retirement is scheduled
Record the avoided operating cost and risk in the program report so the diversion benefit is visible for future cases
Seal connections so the retired site cannot admit inflow or become an unmonitored storage problem

tasks.explanation: Keeping the station restartable until the new route proves itself in a storm is the prudence step. Updating emergency plans matters because a retired station left on call lists wastes the first hour of a real event.

tasks.prompt: Order the fleet spare pumps and critical spares strategy.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: a pump failure at a critical station waited nine days for parts, and spares holdings grew without a method.

cards.label: Store, exercise, and maintain spares so they work when called, with the checks recorded like installed equipment
Confirm interchangeability so a spare pump truly fits the stations it is held for, including connections and controls
List the failure modes that stop a station, including pumps, controls, valves, and power components, by station class
Set the reorder and repair loop so a used spare is repaired or replaced at once, not at the next budget
Set spares by consequence and lead time, stocking what a critical station cannot wait for and sharing the rest across the fleet
Review holdings after every major failure and annually against the fleet standardization progress

tasks.explanation: A spare that does not fit or does not run is inventory, not readiness. The repair loop after use is the step that keeps the strategy true a year later.

tasks.prompt: Order a risk based CCTV inspection program for the whole network.

tasks.configuration: Scope: the utility has 1400 km of sewers, inspection history is uneven, and leadership must set cycles that find failure before it happens.

cards.label: Schedule the first cycle to clear the unknown condition reaches in high consequence locations before reinspecting known good pipe
Feed grades directly into the renewal triggers and the risk register, not into a separate report that planning never sees
Divide the network into risk tiers using age, material, failure history, and consequence of failure by location
Review tier assignments annually as failures, repairs, and new grades change the risk picture
Set inspection cycle lengths per tier, with the highest risk reaches inspected most often and low risk reaches on a long cycle
Grade every inspection to the utility standard with quality checks on a sample so grades are comparable between crews and years

tasks.explanation: Unknown pipe in a high consequence location outranks known good pipe for inspection. Quality checked grading matters because the whole renewal program spends money on these grades.

tasks.prompt: Order a sewer risk register review at senior level.

tasks.configuration: Scope: the risk register lists 60 collection risks, several have sat unchanged for years, and leadership must confirm the register reflects reality.

cards.label: Retire risks that treatment has genuinely closed, with the verification evidence attached
Test each top risk against recent evidence, including failures, inspections, and near misses since it was last scored
Set the review date and the interim triggers that would rescore a risk between reviews, such as a collapse or overflow
Confirm every high risk has a funded treatment or an explicit acceptance signed at the right level
Add new risks the evidence raises, including any location with repeated events not yet on the register
Rescore likelihood and consequence with the evidence in the room, and record where scores change and why

tasks.explanation: A register that never changes is decoration. Signed acceptance for untreated high risks is essential, because silent acceptance hides the decision from the board.

tasks.prompt: Order the program for sewers under critical surface infrastructure.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: major sewers pass under a hospital, a rail line, and arterial roads, where a collapse would be a civic emergency.

cards.label: Inspect those reaches on the shortest cycle with methods that measure remaining wall and deformation, not only pictures
Report the condition of critical crossings to senior leadership annually as a named risk item
Agree access and notification arrangements with the infrastructure owners before an emergency forces the conversation
List every reach whose failure would affect critical infrastructure, using consequence mapping rather than pipe size alone
Set intervention triggers tighter than for ordinary pipe, so repair happens while trenchless methods are still possible
Keep repair readiness for these reaches, including designs or method statements prepared in advance

tasks.explanation: Consequence, not diameter, defines criticality. Preparing designs in advance is what makes intervention possible inside the window trenchless repair needs.

tasks.prompt: Order a root intrusion management program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: roots cause a third of blockages in treed older districts, cutting treats the symptom, and some reaches reblock within a year.

cards.label: Advise property owners where roots enter through laterals, with the options and responsibilities stated plainly
Apply cutting and treatment on cycles matched to regrowth, with the fastest reaches treated before blockage, not after
Classify reaches by regrowth speed from repeat records, separating fast regrowth reaches from occasional intrusions
Program joint sealing or lining for reaches where treatment cycles shorten, because the entry points are the disease
Map root blockages from work records against tree cover, pipe material, and joint condition to find the true pattern
Track blockage rate per district as the program measure and adjust cycles where the rate does not fall

tasks.explanation: Cycles matched to measured regrowth replace both neglect and blanket treatment. Lining the worst reaches ends the cycle where chemistry and cutting only rent relief.

tasks.prompt: Order a fats, oils and grease program at utility scale.

tasks.configuration: Scope: grease blockages cluster around food districts, two overflows last year were grease caused, and the current program is complaint driven.

cards.label: Report blockage and overflow trend in the target catchments as the program measure each year
Set the inspection and education cycle for food premises by risk, with repeat problem sites visited most often
Escalate repeat non compliance through the utility enforcement path, with warnings and evidence in order
Require and verify grease control equipment where the program rules provide for it, with records kept per premises
Clean the affected mains on a frequency set by measured regrowth of deposits, and record the depth found each time
Map grease blockages and cleaning findings to food premises by catchment so the program targets sources, not streets

tasks.explanation: Targeting premises rather than streets is what makes a grease program a source program. Cleaning frequency set by measured deposit regrowth keeps the mains ahead of the sources while enforcement catches up.

tasks.prompt: Order a corrosion and odour risk program for the system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. cards.label: Map the corrosion risk from detention times, force main discharges, temperature, and inspection evidence of crown loss
Program structural protection or renewal for structures whose remaining life the corrosion has already consumed
Review the program each year against remaining life gained at the treated structures
Measure sulfide and corrosion state at the worst locations so treatment is sized from data, not from complaint volume
Track corrosion rate and odour complaints together, because a fix that saves pipe but spreads odour is not a fix
Apply controls in order, from operational changes and ventilation to chemical treatment at the points the data support

tasks.explanation: Detention and discharge points predict corrosion better than complaints do. Tracking asset life and odour together prevents solving one by exporting the other.

tasks.prompt: Order the condition program for large diameter sewers.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. cards.label: Plan each inspection with flow management, safety entry provisions, and the measurement outputs required before crews mobilize
Set the reassessment cycle per reach from the deterioration found, not from a single fleet wide interval
Prioritize by consequence and by time since last assessment, with never assessed critical reaches first
Convert findings into remaining life and intervention options per reach for the capital plan, with urgency stated
List the large diameter inventory with access points, flow depths, and the inspection methods each reach can physically accept
Combine methods per reach, such as sonar below the flow line and laser or visual assessment above it where justified

tasks.explanation: Large sewers need method matched to access and flow, planned before mobilization. Cycles set from observed deterioration keep the most critical assets from becoming the least known.

tasks.prompt: Order a manhole condition and inflow program for river valley areas.

tasks.configuration: Scope: valley manholes sit in flood prone ground, covers and chimneys admit surface water, and several structures are deteriorating.

cards.label: Remeter completed basins in comparable storms and record the change against the work done
Inspect valley structures during and after wet weather so inflow paths are seen working, not guessed from dry stains
Complete repairs basin by basin with sealed covers and raised frames where flooding, not leakage, is the path
Set the reinspection cycle for valley structures shorter than upland, reflecting flood exposure
Rank repairs by inflow removed and flood risk, grouping them by sub basin so flow effect can be measured
Grade each structure for cover, frame, chimney, wall, and benching defects with the repair each grade implies

tasks.explanation: Wet weather inspection finds inflow that dry inspection misses. Basin by basin completion with remeasurement proves the program removes water, not just defects.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a sewer collapse risk found by inspection.

tasks.configuration: Scope: CCTV shows a reach with severe deformation and soil visible, under a busy street, with collapse judged possible within months.

cards.label: Confirm the extent with a focused reinspection or excavation assessment so the repair length is based on evidence
Complete the repair and verify by post repair inspection before the risk is downgraded in the register
Install interim controls, including flow monitoring, cleaning limits, and a bypass plan ready to deploy
Restrict loading and notify the road authority at once if the surface shows any sign of movement or voiding
Review nearby reaches of the same age and material for the same defect pattern before closing the episode
Decide repair method by urgency and access, from internal structural repair to open cut, with traffic and service effects stated

tasks.explanation: Surface safety comes before diagnosis when soil is already entering the pipe. Checking sibling reaches matters because one collapse grade defect usually signals a family of them.

tasks.prompt: Order a data driven cleaning program reset.

tasks.configuration: Scope: cleaning has run on fixed cycles for years, some reaches are cleaned clean while problem reaches reblock between visits.

cards.label: Direct the released capacity to the problem classes and to pre inspection cleaning where grades depend on it
Remove or lengthen cycles on reaches repeatedly found clean, and record the capacity released
Analyse blockage, cleaning findings, and CCTV records together to classify every reach by how fast deposits and roots return
Record findings at every clean in the standard format so the classification improves with each visit
Set cleaning frequencies per class from the measured return rates, with problem reaches cleaned before blockage is expected
Review blockage rate and cost per kilometre annually and reclassify reaches whose behaviour has changed

tasks.explanation: Fixed cycles clean clean pipes and miss dirty ones with equal reliability. Reclassification from findings makes the program smarter every year instead of repeating its first guess.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual operating budget build for the collection utility.

tasks.configuration: Scope: the operating budget must cover crews, fleet, energy, chemicals, and contracted services for the coming year.

cards.label: Separate base operations from growth, new programs, and one time items so each can be judged on its own merits
Present the budget with cost per kilometre and per connection trends so the board sees efficiency, not only totals
Start from the work program, including cleaning, inspection, station maintenance, and response volumes the service levels require
Track spending against the work delivered monthly, reporting variance as work done or not done, not only dollars
Price the work from actual unit costs of the last two years, adjusted for known price and staffing changes
Test the draft against service outcomes, naming what would not get done at lower funding levels

tasks.explanation: A budget built from the work program can explain itself line by line. Reporting variance as work delivered keeps underspending from masquerading as efficiency when it is really service quietly dropped.

tasks.prompt: Order a rate study presentation for wastewater services.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: the utility must fund operations, renewal, and growth, and council must choose a rate path for the next five years.

cards.label: Test affordability honestly, including the effect on typical household bills stated in plain figures
Establish the revenue need from the operating budget, the capital plan, and reserve policy over the study period
Set the annual review that compares actual need and collections with the study and adjusts before gaps compound
Model rate paths from steady annual increases to deferred sharp increases, with the backlog and risk path of each
Recommend a path that funds the adopted service levels and records the risk accepted if council chooses a lower path
Show the current rate position, including how much of renewal is funded today and how much is deferred to the future

tasks.explanation: Deferral is a rate path too, and the study must show its backlog cost. Recording the risk of a lower path protects both council and the utility when the deferred work comes due.

tasks.prompt: Order the board report after a major overflow event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: a storm overflow discharged to a creek for six hours, media attention is high, and the board meets in one week.

cards.label: Explain the cause chain honestly, separating weather severity from system condition and response performance
Commit the follow up report date at which corrective action progress and monitoring results return to the board
Present the corrective actions with owners, funding, and dates, including any that need board approval
State the facts first, including when it started, how long it lasted, the estimated volume, and what was done
Report the environmental and public health actions taken, including sampling, signage, and notifications made
State what the event changes in the risk register, the capital plan, and the wet weather service level discussion

tasks.explanation: Facts before explanation is the order that preserves credibility. A committed follow up date prevents the report from being the end of the accountability it describes.

tasks.prompt: Order a funding application for a major collection project.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: a senior government funding program offers cost sharing for renewal and climate resilience work, with a short application window.

cards.label: Submit with time to correct defects in the application, and keep the full submission record
Confirm the utility share is funded or fundable, and state the operating cost the project creates after construction
Assemble the evidence the application scores on, including condition data, risk, service benefit, and readiness to proceed
Secure the required council or board endorsement before submission, with the project scope matching the approved capital plan
Confirm the project fits the program terms exactly, including eligible costs, timelines, and the outcomes the program funds
If funded, set the reporting and milestone tracking the agreement requires before design money is spent

tasks.explanation: Fit to program terms comes before writing, because strong projects fail on eligibility. Confirming the utility share and future operating cost prevents winning a grant the utility cannot complete.

tasks.prompt: Order the utility response to an audit of its financial reserves.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: an audit finds the renewal reserve is below policy and past councils were not told the gap in plain terms.

cards.label: Report the reserve position in every annual financial report against the policy line until it is restored
Explain how the gap arose, year by year, separating rate decisions, spending changes, and growth in the asset base
Have the board adopt the path and the reporting, with the decision recorded
Present the recovery options with the rate and risk consequences of each, over a stated period
Recommend a recovery path and a plain annual reserve report so the position can never again drift unseen
Verify the reserve position and the policy requirement from the financial records before responding to any finding

tasks.explanation: A gap explained year by year can be governed, a gap presented as a surprise cannot. Annual reporting against the policy line is the control that makes the recovery permanent.

tasks.prompt: Order the procurement strategy for a multi year CCTV and cleaning contract.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: contracted inspection and cleaning cover half the program, the current contract expires, and quality has varied between crews.

cards.label: Define the work and quality standard precisely, including grading accuracy, data format, and production evidence required
Evaluate bids on quality method and past accuracy as well as price, using the scoring published in the tender
Manage performance with monthly quality and production reporting and a stated remedy path for repeated failure
Choose the contract length and packaging so the market can bid competitively and the utility can change course if quality fails
Start the contract with a measured pilot length whose grades are verified before full production is authorized
Set payment tied to accepted deliverables, with inspection data rejected and redone when it fails the quality sample

tasks.explanation: Payment for accepted data, not footage submitted, aligns the contract with its purpose. A verified pilot length catches a weak contractor while the cost of exit is still small.

tasks.prompt: Order a workforce plan for the collection utility.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: retirements, growth, and new programs will change staffing needs over five years, and recruitment for operators is slow.

cards.label: Set the hiring and training lead times so recruitment starts early enough for slow to fill qualifications
Review the plan annually against actual retirements, hiring results, and program delivery
Map current staff against the need, including certifications, confined space qualifications, and single person dependencies
Fund the plan inside the operating budget with the training and backfill cost shown, not hidden
Forecast the work volumes by program and convert them into crew and skill needs year by year
Build internal progression so junior operators can qualify upward, reducing dependence on a tight external market

tasks.explanation: Skill needs with long lead times fail when hiring starts at the vacancy. Internal progression is both a retention tool and the most reliable supply of qualified operators.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual report to council on collection system state.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: council receives one state of the system report each year and uses it to set rates and capital priorities.

cards.label: Ask for the specific rate and capital decisions the report supports, each tied to the evidence presented
Present asset condition honestly, including the share of the network in poor condition and the trend over five years
State the coming need, including the projects and programs that cannot be deferred without named consequences
Publish the report in the same structure each year so council can compare across years without relearning the format
Show what the last year funding delivered in renewed length, risk removed, and flow reduction, with evidence
Report service performance, including overflows, backups, and response results against the adopted service levels

tasks.explanation: Same structure each year is what turns reports into oversight. Asking for specific decisions tied to evidence respects council time and makes deferral an explicit choice.

tasks.prompt: Order the governance of a major capital project from approval to close.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a trunk renewal project is approved at a large budget, delivery will take three years, and past projects drifted without board visibility.

cards.label: Require change control so scope or budget changes return to the approver with the reason and the effect stated
Verify benefits after completion, including condition gained and risk removed, against the original case
Report progress quarterly against the baseline, including forecast final cost, not only spending to date
Set the project baseline at approval, including scope, budget, schedule, and the benefits the project must deliver
Close the project with a lessons review filed where future project teams will find it
Hold stage gates at design completion and tender award where the board can still change course at reasonable cost

tasks.explanation: Forecast final cost, not spending to date, is the number that prevents late surprises. Benefit verification after completion closes the loop that approval opened.

tasks.prompt: Order a mutual aid agreement for wastewater emergencies.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: neighbouring utilities can lend crews, bypass pumps, and vacuum trucks, but no written agreement exists and past help was arranged by phone.

cards.label: Agree communications and command arrangements so visiting crews work inside the host utility safety and direction system
Set liability, insurance, and cost recovery terms in advance with legal review, not during an emergency
Define the events and request process the agreement covers, including who can request and who can approve aid
Sign the agreement and brief dispatch and senior operators in every party on how to activate it
List the resources each party can offer, with rates, operator requirements, and the limits of what will be lent
Exercise the agreement in a joint scenario within the first year and correct what the exercise exposes

tasks.explanation: Terms settled in advance are what make aid fast when it matters. An exercise within the first year proves the phone numbers, paperwork, and command fit before a real night tests them.

tasks.prompt: Order the utility response leadership for a major trunk sewer failure.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a trunk sewer has collapsed under an arterial road at the start of a storm, flows are rising, and the event will run for days.

cards.label: Control the flow, deploying bypass pumping and storage to prevent or limit overflow while repair options are assessed
Choose the repair path under command, balancing speed, safety, and durability, with the decision and reasons recorded
Establish incident command with a named lead, defined roles, and a single point for decisions and records
Stand down in stages as flow is restored, then complete the event review and the corrective actions it identifies
Protect the public first, including road closure, site control, and warnings for any affected properties
Notify the regulator, public health contacts, and the public in general terms as procedures require, with facts as they are confirmed

tasks.explanation: Command and public protection precede repair choice in a multi day event. Recording decisions as they are made is what makes the later review evidence rather than recollection.

tasks.prompt: Order a flood season readiness program for the collection system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: spring melt and storm season approach, several areas flood predictably, and readiness has depended on individual memory.

cards.label: Confirm staffing rosters, call out arrangements, and mutual aid contacts for the season and brief every shift
List the known flood and surcharge locations with the trigger conditions and past performance at each
Review readiness after the first event of the season and correct gaps while the season still has time to use them
Pre position equipment and materials at the locations the record supports, including pumps, hose, and sandbag supplies
Set the monitoring and communication routine for events, including who updates leadership and the public and how often
Inspect and service the critical assets before the season, including stations, generators, gates, and known constriction points

tasks.explanation: Readiness built from the location record beats generic preparation. Reviewing after the first event uses a real test while correction still matters.

tasks.prompt: Order the leadership of a multi day bypass pumping operation.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a trunk repair requires bypassing full flow for five days, including nights and a forecast storm inside the window.

cards.label: Secure the site, including traffic control, noise and odour management for neighbours, and safe fuel handling and storage
Demobilize in stages after the repair passes inspection, keeping bypass ready until normal flow is proven stable
Define the storm trigger at which work pauses and the system is returned to the safest state, before the storm arrives
Size the bypass for peak wet weather flow with standby capacity, not for average flow, and prove it by test pumping
Set the watch rotation and alarm coverage so the bypass is attended or monitored continuously, with relief crews scheduled
Communicate daily with affected residents and the regulator contact on progress, incidents, and the expected end

tasks.explanation: Peak flow sizing with standby capacity is the difference between a bypass and a hope. A pre set storm trigger removes the worst decision from the worst moment.

tasks.prompt: Order an emergency exercise program for collection events.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plans exist for overflows, station failures, and collapses, but only one has ever been exercised and new staff have joined since.

cards.label: Correct the plans, equipment, and training the findings identify, and retest the failed steps specifically
Progress to a field exercise for the most critical scenario, with real equipment deployment and timing measured
Run tabletop exercises first to test decisions, notifications, and records without field cost
Record findings as specific failed or slow steps, each with an owner and a correction date
Choose scenarios from the real risk register, starting with the highest consequence events the utility actually faces
Set the exercise cycle so every major scenario is tested on a rotation and after any real event that exposed a gap

tasks.explanation: Scenarios from the risk register keep exercises honest rather than theatrical. Retesting the failed steps is the step that separates an exercise program from an exercise event.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a hazardous spill entering the collection system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a fuel spill has entered a storm connected area and may reach sanitary sewers and a lift station, creating explosion and treatment risks.

cards.label: Inspect and clear affected structures before normal operation resumes, and complete the event record and review
Identify the material and quantity from the source and responders so downstream decisions rest on facts
Recover contaminated material with qualified support and dispose of it through the approved route
Contain what can be contained at entry points and protect the lift station and treatment plant by isolation where possible
Notify the regulator, fire service, and treatment operations in general terms as procedures require, with the material facts
Protect people first, including ventilation awareness, ignition control, and keeping crews out of affected structures until assessed

tasks.explanation: Explosion risk governs the first hour, so entry waits for assessment. Early warning to treatment operations protects a second facility from a problem it did not create.

tasks.prompt: Order the winter storm emergency response for the collection system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a severe cold snap with heavy snow is forecast, access will be difficult, and several stations have frozen in past events.

cards.label: Issue the readiness check before the storm, covering station heat, fuel, access clearing priorities, and crew availability
Monitor alarms centrally and dispatch on priority, conserving crew travel in dangerous conditions
Review the event after thaw, including any freeze damage found late, and update the cold weather procedures
Set the priority list for station checks during the event, ordered by overflow consequence and freeze history
Communicate with leadership and the public on service status at set intervals during the event
Arrange snow clearing for critical station access as part of the response, not as an afterthought

tasks.explanation: Access is an operational system in a winter storm, planned like pumping. The post thaw review catches the damage the storm hid, which is when freeze failures often appear.

tasks.prompt: Order the public communication during a prolonged overflow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: an overflow to a recreational creek will continue for at least two days while a repair is completed.

cards.label: Publish a plain language statement of what happened, what is being done, and when the next update will come
Close the event publicly when monitoring supports it, remove signage, and publish the final summary and corrective actions
Notify public health contacts and the regulator in general terms as procedures require, and confirm the notifications in the record
Sample and monitor as the response plan requires and share results when they are confirmed, not as preliminary numbers
Post the affected area notices at once, including access points, trails, and any water use the health guidance covers
Update on the promised schedule even when the news is only that work continues, so silence does not fill with rumour

tasks.explanation: Updates on schedule, even without new facts, hold public trust through a long event. Closing publicly with the corrective actions completes the accountability the first notice began.

tasks.prompt: Order the recovery phase after a major collection emergency.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the immediate event is over, crews are fatigued, temporary repairs are in place, and normal service is not yet fully restored.

cards.label: Complete the cost, event, and regulatory records while the detail is fresh, including all notifications made
Confirm life safety and environmental controls are stable before shifting attention to restoration
Rest crews and rotate staff, because fatigue in the recovery week causes the second incident
Hold the formal review and assign corrective actions with dates before the episode is closed in the program tracker
Restore permanent service in risk order, verifying each element as it returns so temporary measures retire safely
List every temporary measure in place, including bypasses, plugs, and borrowed equipment, with an owner for each

tasks.explanation: Temporary measures with named owners retire safely, temporary measures without them become permanent by neglect. Crew rest is a safety control in recovery, not a reward.

tasks.prompt: Order the leadership decision during competing simultaneous emergencies.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a storm has caused a station failure, a trunk surcharge with backups, and a road collapse at the same time, and crews cannot cover all three at full strength.

cards.label: Rank the events by risk to life first, then environmental harm, then property damage, and state the ranking openly
Reassess the ranking as events change, moving resources when a holding action starts to fail
Assign the strongest resources to the highest risk event and give the others holding actions that limit harm
Establish one command point that sees all three events and owns the allocation of crews and equipment
Record the allocation decisions and reasons for the review that will follow the storm
Tell affected parties honestly what response they will get and when, rather than promising full response everywhere

tasks.explanation: One command point prevents three separate responses from stripping each other of resources. Honest communication about response levels protects trust better than promises the crews cannot keep.

tasks.prompt: Order the after action review for a significant overflow event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a significant overflow occurred last month, reports are filed, and leadership must convert the event into system improvement.

cards.label: Assign corrective actions with owners, funding routes, and dates, sized to what the budget can actually carry
Identify the causes in order, from the immediate trigger to the program gaps that let it matter
Rebuild the timeline from records, alarms, and crew accounts while memories are still checkable against data
Add or rescore the risk register entries the event informs, including any location now known to be fragile
Separate what the system did by design from what individuals improvised, so credit and blame land accurately
Track the actions in the CMOM review until verification, not intention, closes each one

tasks.explanation: Separating design from improvisation shows whether the plan or the people carried the day. Tracking to verification keeps the review from becoming the place corrective actions go to be forgotten.

tasks.prompt: Order the leadership of an overflow reporting and compliance review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the utility reported twelve overflows last year, leadership must confirm each was reported correctly and on time under provincial requirements in general terms.

cards.label: Correct any late or incomplete filings through the proper channel and record what caused the failure
Brief senior leadership on the compliance position with the corrective actions and owners stated
Reconcile the overflow list from field records, alarms, and reports filed, and investigate any event in one source but not the others
Sample the next quarter reports independently so the fix is verified, not assumed
Check each report for timeliness, completeness, and the volume estimation method used
Fix the reporting workflow where the failures cluster, including after hours steps and volume estimation guidance

tasks.explanation: Reconciliation across sources is how unreported events are found. Independent sampling next quarter proves the workflow change rather than trusting it.

tasks.prompt: Order the preparation for a provincial regulatory inspection of the collection system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the provincial regulator will inspect the collection system next month, covering records, overflow history, and program documentation in general terms.

cards.label: Walk the critical sites the inspector is likely to visit and correct housekeeping and safety issues found
Confirm the inspection scope and prepare the records the scope names, organized as the utility actually uses them
Convert the inspection findings into tracked corrective actions and report progress to leadership until closed
Brief the staff who will host the inspection on answering factually and producing records, not on defending positions
Host the inspection with a senior lead present, recording every request and commitment made during the visit
Review the records honestly for gaps before the visit and list what cannot be produced, with the reason for each

tasks.explanation: Gaps listed honestly before the visit are manageable, gaps discovered by the inspector are findings. Recording commitments made during the visit prevents casual remarks becoming missed obligations.

tasks.prompt: Order the senior decision on a consent or compliance schedule for wet weather overflows.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the regulator proposes a compliance schedule requiring overflow reduction milestones over ten years, and the utility must respond.

cards.label: Test the proposed milestones against the I/I and capacity programs to see what is achievable with funded work
Track milestone progress in the CMOM review and warn leadership early when any milestone is at risk
Negotiate from the evidence, seeking milestones the funded program can meet and committing only to what can be delivered
Establish the utility actual overflow baseline from reconciled records so negotiations rest on verified history
Cost the accelerated work any tighter milestone would require, with given rates, and state the rate effect
Have the board adopt the final schedule, understanding the legal and funding commitment it creates

tasks.explanation: Commitments made beyond the funded program become breaches on a schedule. Early warning inside the program review is what gives leadership time to act before a milestone is missed.

tasks.prompt: Order the decision framework for approving a new technology for the collection system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: vendors propose new inspection, lining, and monitoring technologies regularly, and past adoptions were uneven in result.

cards.label: Decide adoption, limited use, or rejection in a written record that future proposals can be judged against
Run a bounded pilot with acceptance criteria set in advance and city staff recording the results
Require evidence from comparable utilities, including climate and system similarity, not only vendor references
Compare the pilot results with the current method on cost, quality, and risk using given rates
Define the problem the technology must solve in measurable terms before any trial is discussed
If adopted, set the training, specification, and quality checks that make the technology perform as piloted

tasks.explanation: Criteria set before the pilot cannot drift to fit the result. A written decision record stops rejected technologies returning every few years as if new.

tasks.prompt: Order the senior review of a proposed sewer use bylaw update.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the sewer use rules need updating for grease, prohibited discharges, and hauled waste, and council must approve the changes.

cards.label: Measure blockage and discharge trends after adoption and report whether the rules changed the behaviour they targeted
Draft the provisions with legal review, in plain language that premises owners and haulers can actually follow
Present the update to council with the evidence, the consultation results, and the enforcement cost stated
Consult affected users, including food premises and haulers, and record the concerns that change the draft
Set the enforcement and education plan that launches with the rules, including inspection capacity and grace periods
Document the problems the update must solve from blockage, spill, and treatment impact records

tasks.explanation: Rules written for the records that justify them survive challenge. Launching enforcement and education together is what turns a bylaw from paper into changed discharges.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a treatment plant request to limit wet weather flows.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the treatment plant, operated by the same utility, asks collection to cap peak deliveries that are stressing plant processes in storms.

cards.label: Quantify the current peak delivery pattern and the plant limit from joint operating records, in flows and durations
Set an interim operating protocol for major storms with named decision makers on both sides
Review joint performance after each season and adjust the protocol and the program priorities together
Agree the shared objective, including the overflow risk that capping shifts back into the collection system
Fund the agreed works in both programs so the protocol is a bridge to a fix, not a permanent argument
Evaluate the collection options, including storage, I/I priorities near the plant, and staged delivery using existing assets

tasks.explanation: Capping flow moves risk rather than removing it, so both sides own the trade off. A protocol with named decision makers prevents the storm night negotiation this arrangement usually becomes.

tasks.prompt: Order the leadership review of operator certification and staffing compliance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: collection operations require certified operators at the right levels under provincial requirements in general terms, and retirements threaten coverage.

cards.label: Identify the gaps by date, including retirements and certifications in progress that may not complete in time
Report coverage as a standing item in the program review so a gap is never discovered by an inspector first
Compare current staff certifications against the requirement, including vacation, sickness, and vacancy coverage
Confirm the records that prove coverage are kept current and can be produced on request
List the positions and shifts that require certified coverage and the level each requires in general terms
Fund the training, examination, and backfill path that closes each gap before its date

tasks.explanation: Coverage checked only on full staffing fails at the first vacation. Standing review keeps certification a managed pipeline rather than a recurring surprise.

tasks.prompt: Order the evaluation of a public private delivery option for a major project.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a major trunk project could be delivered conventionally or through an alternative delivery model, and the board wants a defensible comparison.

cards.label: Recommend the model with the comparison recorded so the decision can be revisited if conditions change
Define the project outcomes and risk allocation the utility needs before comparing delivery models
Assess the utility ability to manage the contract each model creates, including staff skills and oversight cost
Set the governance and reporting for the chosen model before procurement begins
Test the market honestly, including how many qualified bidders each model would actually attract
Compare models on whole life cost with given rates, including the cost of risks each model transfers or retains

tasks.explanation: Risk transfer has a price, and the comparison must show it. Assessing the utility own contract management capacity prevents choosing a model the organization cannot actually oversee.

tasks.prompt: Order the senior decision when a capital project encounters major cost growth.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: tender prices for a trunk renewal came in 40 percent over estimate, and stopping, rescoping, and proceeding all carry risk.

cards.label: Reconfirm the project need from the condition and risk evidence, since the case for the work may still be strong
Record the decision and reset the baseline so the project is managed against the approved position from that point
Develop the options, including rescope, phasing, retender, and proceed, with the risk and cost of each stated
Verify the tender result, checking bidder spread and whether the estimate or the market moved
Feed the estimating lesson into the capital plan rates so the same surprise is not priced into the next project
Present the options to the board with a recommendation and the consequence of deferral in plain terms

tasks.explanation: A strong need can survive a bad tender, but only a verified one should. Resetting the baseline after the decision restores control instead of managing against a number everyone knows is dead.

tasks.prompt: Order the long term advocacy position on senior government infrastructure funding.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the utility will present its infrastructure needs to senior government funders and industry associations this year.

cards.label: Align the ask with the programs and priorities the funders actually run, without distorting the utility real needs
Show the consequence path of the gap, including service, environmental, and growth effects over time
Build the case from the asset data, including condition, backlog, growth, and climate pressures in verified figures
Present the case consistently through the board chair and senior staff so the message does not vary by audience
State the funding gap honestly, including what current rates fund and what they cannot
Report back what was heard and adjust the capital plan assumptions to the realistic funding outlook

tasks.explanation: Verified figures are the utility credibility with funders. Adjusting plan assumptions to what was actually heard keeps advocacy from becoming a substitute for planning.

tasks.prompt: Order a utility wide winter operations strategy.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: winters bring deep frost, frozen services, and spring melt surges, and each district has handled them differently.

cards.label: Fund the prevention work in the off season, when access is easy and the cost per fix is lowest
Track winter events on one utility basis so districts can be compared and the worst exposures funded first
Compile the winter record across districts, including frozen services, station freeze events, and melt surge performance
Review the strategy after each winter with district leads and carry the corrections into the next off season program
Set the utility standards for winter work, including burial and insulation expectations, station heat checks, and thaw response
Set the melt season readiness routine, including monitoring of known surcharge points and pre positioned equipment

tasks.explanation: Prevention funded in summer is the cheapest winter program there is. One reporting basis across districts is what lets the worst exposures, not the loudest, get funded.

tasks.prompt: Order the frozen service response program for a severe winter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a deep cold period has frozen services across older districts, calls exceed crew capacity, and prioritization must be fair and fast.

cards.label: Track frozen locations precisely, because the same services freeze in the same conditions year after year
Triage calls by vulnerability and by whether the property has any water or sewer function, and record the triage rule used
Program frost protection or renewal for the repeat locations in the off season, funded from the winter record
Set honest wait time communication for residents, updated as the queue moves, rather than optimistic estimates
Restore services in triage order and confirm drainage function, not only water flow, before closing each call
Deploy thawing crews and equipment by district plan, with safety checks for electrical thawing and structure entry

tasks.explanation: Triage by vulnerability keeps a first come system from failing the people most at risk. The precise location record is the asset the bad winter creates, and the off season program is how it pays off.

tasks.prompt: Order the spring melt surge management plan.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: rapid melt over frozen ground drives the highest flows of the year in several sheds, with surcharging in the same areas each spring.

cards.label: Monitor flows and levels from melt onset at the known points so response starts on evidence, not on the first backup call
Record the melt performance shed by shed and fold the results into the I/I and capacity programs
Coordinate with road and drainage crews, because melt water management on the surface changes what reaches the sewers
Identify the melt surge sheds and the trigger conditions from past melt records, including temperature pattern and snowpack
Pre position bypass and cleaning capacity at the locations where melt surcharging has occurred before
Communicate with residents in the known areas before the peak, including what to report and what the utility is doing

tasks.explanation: Melt surge is predictable in place if not in size, so pre positioning beats reaction. Folding results into the I/I program matters because melt inflow and rainfall inflow share many entry points.

tasks.prompt: Order a lift station freeze protection program across the fleet.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: past winters froze discharge piping, vents, and level controls at exposed stations, causing alarms and two overflows.

cards.label: Fit temperature alarming where the consequence justifies it so a heat failure calls for help before the freeze does damage
Correct the defects in priority order, with the stations whose failure overflows fastest corrected first
Inspect the vulnerable stations before winter, testing heat, insulation, ventilation, and alarm function on cold specific checks
Set the winter check frequency per station from its freeze history and consequence, and record every check
List the freeze failures by station and component from the winter records, separating heat loss, exposure, and equipment faults
Review every freeze event in season and adjust checks while the winter can still test the fix

tasks.explanation: Component level records turn winter folklore into a work list. Temperature alarming converts a silent heat failure into a call that arrives in time.

tasks.prompt: Order the winter construction controls for a sewer renewal project.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 4 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a renewal project must continue through winter to meet a road program deadline, with frozen ground, short days, and live flows.

cards.label: Plan the spring verification, including inspection of winter placed work after thaw for settlement and joint defects
Set the flow management for winter storms and melt pulses, with bypass capacity and freeze protection for bypass lines
Increase inspection presence on the cold sensitive steps, because winter defects hide until thaw
Define the quality checks that cold changes, including material temperatures, curing protection, and compaction testing limits
Agree the stop work triggers for extreme cold and storm conditions before the season, not during an event
Confirm the winter work plan with the contractor, including excavation support in frozen ground and bedding and compaction methods for cold conditions

tasks.explanation: Winter defects announce themselves at thaw, so spring verification is part of the winter plan. Stop work triggers agreed in advance protect both quality and crews when conditions turn.

tasks.configuration: Scope: frost depths have reached design burial in recent winters, several new services froze, and the construction standard is under review.

Apply the standard to new approvals at once and record any variance granted with its reason and risk
Review freeze performance under the new standard after each severe winter and adjust if the evidence requires
Compare the current standard with the observed frost penetration and with the practice of comparable cold climate utilities
Advise owners of existing shallow services on protection options where renewal is not planned
Set the revised burial, insulation, and material provisions by soil and exposure type, not as one depth for all ground

tasks.explanation: Evidence by soil and exposure beats a single deeper depth everywhere. Recording variances keeps exceptions visible instead of quietly rebuilding the old problem.

tasks.prompt: Order the management of ice affected manholes and access in winter operations.

Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: crews lose hours to frozen covers and snow buried structures during winter emergencies, and one response was delayed at a critical station access.

cards.label: Fit or maintain cover features that resist freezing where the record shows repeated seizure, and keep the tools for safe opening on the trucks
Review the priority list after each winter against the delays actually recorded
Mark and record those locations for snow clearing priority and include them in the winter route plans
Track access delays during winter events as an operational measure, not as bad luck
Identify the structures and accesses that winter response cannot afford to lose, from the emergency and station priority lists
Brief crews on safe opening methods that avoid injury and cover damage in frozen conditions

tasks.prompt: Order an energy and heat audit for winter station operating costs.

tasks.configuration: Scope: heating and freeze protection are a large winter cost at remote stations, and spending varies widely between similar sites.

Set temperature standards by station need, protecting equipment and access without heating empty space to comfort levels
Reinvest part of the verified saving in the freeze protection program so efficiency funds reliability
Correct the building and equipment causes first, including insulation, seals, and controls that hold set temperatures
Inspect the high cost stations for heat loss, oversized or failed equipment, and ventilation that discards heated air

Record volumes and durations at monitored interfaces so the I/I program can price their removal honestly
Set the melt season watch at the remaining interfaces, with level monitoring and response triggers agreed in advance

Report the interface results in the annual wet weather review with the remaining points ranked for correction
Coordinate with the stormwater service on surface flooding response so each crew knows which water belongs to which system
