tasks.prompt: A utility director reviews a five year inflow and infiltration strategy in Calgary where total wet weather volume fell but basement backup reports did not.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian utility scale inflow and infiltration strategy review. Flows, rainfall, groundwater and costs are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Total wet weather volume at the plant falls 18 percent over five years of lining and disconnection work.
Basement backup reports stay flat over the same five years and cluster in two low basins.
Flow monitors in the two backup basins show peak rates still above their trunk sewer capacity at a 25 mm storm.
Citywide volume is dominated by three large basins where peaks fell well below trunk capacity.
Rainfall totals and storm counts are similar in the first and last strategy years.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The strategy cut total volume where capacity was already adequate, while the two backup basins still exceed local trunk capacity at moderate storms
The strategy failed everywhere, which the falling total volume also shows
Backups persist because residents in the two basins use more water than the city average
Wetter weather in the last year explains both the flat backups and the falling volume

inference.explanation: Volume and local peak capacity are different problems. The citywide gain is real, but the two basins still surcharge at 25 mm, so backups persist there.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Declare the strategy complete because total wet weather volume fell 18 percent
Rebalance the next strategy phase toward peak reduction in the two surcharge basins, and judge it on local peak rates, not citywide volume alone
Repeat the same lining program in the three large basins where peaks already fell

nextClue.explanation: Local peak capacity, not total volume, is the constraint behind the remaining backups.

clueText.nc-a: A volume target alone already hid the local surcharge problem for five years.
clueText.nc-b: The rebalance ranks basins by peak rate against trunk capacity and funds the two surcharging basins first.
clueText.nc-c: More work where peaks are already below capacity cannot relieve the two surcharging trunks.

tasks.prompt: An Edmonton utility compares two ten year strategies on paper: full basin renewal in six basins, or targeted peak shaving plus storage in the same six basins.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian utility scale inflow and infiltration strategy review. Flows, rainfall, groundwater and costs are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Modelled results use the same rainfall series, growth forecast and trunk capacities for both options.
Full renewal removes more total volume but leaves two basins above trunk capacity at the design storm.
Targeted peak shaving plus storage brings all six basins below trunk capacity at the design storm.
Full renewal costs 2.4 times the targeted option over ten years in the same cost model.
Overflow and backup history in the six basins is driven by peak surcharge events, not by total annual volume.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Full renewal is the better strategy because it removes the most total volume
Neither option can be compared because they were modelled differently
Full renewal costs less because renewal avoids all future maintenance
On the shared model, the targeted option meets the capacity test in all six basins at lower cost, while full renewal still fails the test in two basins

inference.explanation: Same model, same storm: one option passes the capacity test everywhere and costs less, the other fails in two basins despite removing more volume.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Advance the targeted option for detailed design, keeping the shared model and design storm as the comparison basis
Advance full renewal because removing the most volume is the safest test of success
Restart the comparison with a different rainfall series for each option

nextClue.explanation: A strategy is judged against the failure mode it must prevent, which here is peak surcharge.

clueText.nc-a: Detailed design proceeds on the targeted option with the design storm results tabled basin by basin.
clueText.nc-b: Total volume removed does not fix a basin that still surcharges at the design storm.
clueText.nc-c: Different rainfall series would make the two options impossible to compare fairly.

tasks.prompt: A Winnipeg utility finds its inflow and infiltration budget has been allocated by pipe length for a decade, and a new flow based allocation is tested on one year of data.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian utility scale inflow and infiltration strategy review. Flows, rainfall, groundwater and costs are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Basins with the most pipe length hold newer gasketed pipe and show the lowest measured inflow per kilometre.
Two short older basins show the highest measured inflow per kilometre and most overflow events.
Under length based allocation, the two high inflow basins received the smallest shares of last year budget.
Under flow based allocation in the test year, the same total budget shifts most funding to the two high inflow basins.
Meter verification and rainfall matching are consistent across all basins in the test year.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Pipe length is the fairest allocator because every basin has pipe to maintain
The two short basins show high inflow because their meters are the newest in the system
Length based allocation has been sending the least money to the basins with the most measured inflow, so allocation should follow measured flow, not pipe length
Overflow events in the short basins are unrelated to their measured inflow

inference.explanation: Verified matched data show need concentrated in the short basins while funding followed length. The allocator, not the basins, produced the mismatch.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Keep length based allocation and add a small bonus to the two high inflow basins
Allocate the whole budget to the two high inflow basins and stop work elsewhere
Adopt flow based allocation for the strategy budget, with meter verification repeated before each allocation cycle

nextClue.explanation: Allocation rules decide outcomes as surely as construction does, and this rule inverted need and funding.

clueText.nc-a: A small bonus leaves the inverted rule in place and the high inflow basins still underfunded.
clueText.nc-b: Concentrating everything ignores moderate needs elsewhere and the staged nature of basin programs.
clueText.nc-c: Flow based allocation is adopted with a verification step before each cycle so funding follows current measured need.

tasks.prompt: A Regina strategy review asks whether private side inflow should be tackled before or after public side renewal, using paired basin results from two completed phases.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian utility scale inflow and infiltration strategy review. Flows, rainfall, groundwater and costs are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: In Basin A, public renewal first cut storm peaks 20 percent, and later private work cut a further 25 percent.
In Basin B, private work first cut storm peaks 25 percent, and later public renewal cut a further 20 percent.
Final peak reductions are nearly identical in the two basins after both stages.
Private work cost per property and public renewal cost per metre were similar in both basins.
Both basins were monitored at matched rainfall with verified meters through both stages.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Private work must always come first, which Basin A disproves by reaching the same endpoint
Order of public and private work did not change the final result in these basins, so sequencing can follow access, cost and coordination rather than a fixed rule
Public renewal must always come first, which Basin B disproves by reaching the same endpoint
One of the two basins must have faulty meters because their stage gains differ in order

inference.explanation: Both orders converge to the same verified endpoint at similar unit costs. Neither fixed rule survives the paired result.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Impose a citywide private first rule on all future basins
Set basin sequence by local access windows, road programs and property participation, and measure each stage as it completes
Impose a citywide public first rule on all future basins

nextClue.explanation: When two orders reach the same measured endpoint, logistics, not doctrine, should set the sequence.

clueText.nc-a: Basin B reached the same endpoint starting with public work, so a private first rule is not supported.
clueText.nc-b: The strategy guide records both paired results and assigns sequence basin by basin on access and coordination.
clueText.nc-c: Basin A reached the same endpoint starting with private work, so a public first rule is not supported.

tasks.prompt: A Saskatoon utility reviews a strategy claim that inflow and infiltration work avoided a trunk sewer upsizing, and checks the capacity file before repeating the claim.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian utility scale inflow and infiltration strategy review. Flows, rainfall, groundwater and costs are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: The trunk design file shows the upsizing was triggered by growth forecasts, not by wet weather peaks.
Wet weather peaks in the trunk fell 30 percent after basin work, verified at matched rainfall.
Growth in the trunk service area came in 40 percent below the forecast used in the design file.
With actual growth and reduced peaks, the existing trunk now meets the design storm with margin.
The original upsizing project was deferred, not cancelled, and remains in the long range plan.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The avoided upsizing claim is only partly supported: lower peaks helped, but slower than forecast growth is the other reason the existing trunk now fits
Basin work alone avoided the upsizing, so the claim should be repeated as written
Basin work contributed nothing, because peaks are irrelevant to trunk capacity
The trunk fits only because its flow meters began under reading after basin work

inference.explanation: Peaks fell and growth undershot together. Crediting either factor alone misstates the record, and the project is deferred, not cancelled.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Report the deferral with both factors stated, and keep the upsizing in the long range plan tied to growth triggers
Report that basin work cancelled the upsizing project permanently
Remove the upsizing from the long range plan because the trunk fits today

nextClue.explanation: Honest attribution keeps a deferral from hardening into a false cancellation.

clueText.nc-a: The report credits peak reduction and lower growth together and sets a growth trigger for revisiting the project.
clueText.nc-b: The project was deferred on a growth forecast, so claiming permanent cancellation misstates the file.
clueText.nc-c: Removing it would leave no planned response if growth returns to forecast rates.

tasks.prompt: A Kelowna utility weighs ending its inflow and infiltration strategy after meeting its original volume target, while overflow records are checked at the same review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian utility scale inflow and infiltration strategy review. Flows, rainfall, groundwater and costs are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: The original strategy target, a 20 percent cut in wet weather volume, is met five years early.
Sanitary overflow events fall from 14 to 11 per year, well short of the utility overflow goal of 4 or fewer.
Remaining overflows concentrate in wet spring weeks when groundwater is highest.
Basins not yet treated hold most of the remaining groundwater driven night flow.
The treatment plant confirms wet weather volume from treated basins did fall as reported.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The strategy should end because its only target has been met
Overflows are unrelated to collection flows, so they should not affect the strategy decision
The plant volume record must be wrong because overflows remain
Meeting the volume target early does not end the strategy, because the overflow goal is unmet and the remaining flow sits in untreated high groundwater basins

inference.explanation: The volume target and the overflow goal measure different outcomes. One is met, the other is not, and the untreated basins explain why.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Close the strategy and transfer its budget to plant upgrades
Keep the volume target unchanged for another five years without new basins
Extend the strategy with an overflow based target aimed at the untreated high groundwater basins

nextClue.explanation: A program ends when its purpose is achieved, not when its first metric is.

clueText.nc-a: Plant upgrades cannot remove groundwater flow entering untreated basins.
clueText.nc-b: Repeating a met target adds no work where the remaining flow actually is.
clueText.nc-c: The extension sets an overflow target and schedules the untreated high groundwater basins next.

tasks.prompt: A Red Deer utility audits whether its strategy spending tracked its own priority ranking, comparing five years of projects to the ranked basin list.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian utility scale inflow and infiltration strategy review. Flows, rainfall, groundwater and costs are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: The ranked list put Basins 3, 5 and 8 first on measured inflow and overflow history.
Five year spending records show 70 percent of strategy funds went to Basins 1 and 2, which ranked ninth and tenth.
Basins 1 and 2 projects were advanced because road reconstruction was already scheduled there.
No documented risk decision records the change in basin order or its effect on overflow goals.
Measured inflow and overflow results in Basins 3, 5 and 8 are unchanged over the five years.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The ranking was wrong, which the road schedule proves
Basins 3, 5 and 8 improved on their own, so the drift caused no harm
Spending drifted from the ranked priorities for road coordination reasons without a documented risk decision, leaving the top ranked basins untreated
Spending records must be misfiled because utilities always follow their rankings

inference.explanation: The funds followed the road program, the top basins show no improvement, and no record justifies the swap. Drift without documentation is the finding.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Ban all coordination with road programs in future strategy work
Require a documented risk decision, with overflow impact stated, before any future reordering of the ranked basin list
Re-rank the basins to match where the money already went

nextClue.explanation: Coordination is legitimate only when its cost to the priority goal is recorded and accepted openly.

clueText.nc-a: Road coordination can be efficient; the failure was the missing decision record, not the coordination itself.
clueText.nc-b: Future reordering needs a signed risk note stating the overflow impact of delaying the ranked basins.
clueText.nc-c: Rewriting the ranking after the fact would hide the drift instead of governing it.

tasks.prompt: A Brandon utility reviews a decade of inflow data and finds total system inflow flat, while its strategy reports claimed steady progress each year.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian utility scale inflow and infiltration strategy review. Flows, rainfall, groundwater and costs are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: System inflow per millimetre of rain is unchanged over ten years when all basins are combined.
Yearly strategy reports summed flow removed by each project without checking for flow returning in later years.
Re-monitoring of three early project basins shows about half their removed flow returned within six years.
Later projects used methods with sealed connections, and their re-monitoring shows removal holding at five years.
Rainfall and groundwater records are complete and consistent across the decade.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The decade record must be wrong because each yearly report showed progress
Reported progress overstated durable removal because early project gains partly returned, so the strategy must count only removal that survives re-monitoring
All removal methods decay equally, which the later project re-monitoring contradicts
Flow returned because population growth added sanitary flow in the early basins

inference.explanation: Yearly sums counted gross removal, re-monitoring shows early gains decaying while sealed connection work holds. Durability, not activity, is the missing test.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Add scheduled re-monitoring to the strategy and report net durable removal by method
Keep reporting gross removal per project as the strategy headline
Stop all lining work because early projects lost some of their gain

nextClue.explanation: A strategy that never re-measures will keep claiming gains the system no longer holds.

clueText.nc-a: Re-monitoring is scheduled at set intervals and the headline becomes net durable removal by method.
clueText.nc-b: Gross removal reporting is exactly what hid the returning flow for a decade.
clueText.nc-c: Later sealed methods held their gains, so the evidence supports fixing methods and measurement, not stopping work.

tasks.prompt: A Prince George utility sets a new inflow and infiltration strategy after a trunk failure review shows wet weather surcharge, not pipe condition, caused the failure.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian utility scale inflow and infiltration strategy review. Flows, rainfall, groundwater and costs are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: The failed trunk section is structurally sound on post failure CCTV, with no collapse or major defect.
Level monitors show the trunk surcharged to the crown for six hours during the failure storm.
Upstream basins delivered peak rates 60 percent above the trunk design rate during that storm.
Two upstream overflow structures operated during the same six hours.
The trunk passes its condition based remaining life assessment with decades of life left.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The failure was a capacity and inflow problem in a sound pipe, so the strategy response belongs in upstream peak reduction, not trunk renewal
The trunk should be renewed first because any failure means the pipe is at end of life
The level monitors must be wrong because the pipe looks sound on camera
The overflow structures caused the trunk to surcharge by operating

inference.explanation: Sound condition, decades of remaining life, and measured surcharge with upstream peaks far above design all point one way. Renewal would replace a good pipe and keep the peaks.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Program full trunk renewal as the first strategy project
Remove the overflow structures so the trunk keeps all flow
Direct the strategy to upstream peak reduction and set trunk level alarms for surcharge warning

nextClue.explanation: Matching the remedy to the failure mechanism is the core strategy skill at this level.

clueText.nc-a: Renewing a sound trunk leaves upstream peaks 60 percent above its design rate unchanged.
clueText.nc-b: Removing overflow relief would raise surcharge and backup risk, not lower it.
clueText.nc-c: Upstream basins are ranked by peak rate and trunk level alarms are set below the crown.

tasks.prompt: A Nanaimo utility compares inflow and infiltration strategy outcomes between its coastal low basins and its upland basins over eight years.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian utility scale inflow and infiltration strategy review. Flows, rainfall, groundwater and costs are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Low basins below the seasonal water table show large night flow gains from joint sealing and lining.
Upland basins above the water table show little night flow change from the same work.
Upland storm peaks fall mainly where roof and drain disconnections were completed.
Low basin storm peaks fall less than their night flows, and disconnection rates there are low.
Methods, crews and unit costs were the same in both areas over the eight years.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: One method is simply better everywhere, and the upland crews applied it poorly
Upland basins have no inflow problem because their night flows did not change
Low basins should stop lining because their storm peaks fell less than night flows
The same methods produced different results by setting: sealing and lining pay in high groundwater basins, while disconnection pays in upland basins

inference.explanation: Matched methods and costs isolate setting as the variable. Each area responded to the route that dominates there: groundwater entry low, direct connections upland.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Apply the low basin lining program unchanged to the upland basins
Split the strategy into two tracks, groundwater entry work for low basins and disconnection work for upland basins, each with its own success measure
Judge both areas on night flow change alone

nextClue.explanation: Strategy at utility scale means matching method to setting, not averaging results across unlike basins.

clueText.nc-a: Upland night flow barely moved under lining, so repeating it there wastes the lesson of eight years.
clueText.nc-b: The two track plan sets night flow targets for low basins and storm peak targets for upland basins.
clueText.nc-c: Night flow alone would score the successful upland disconnection work as failure.

tasks.prompt: A Nanaimo utility reviews winter staffing after a storm season in which crews worked long overtime and inspection backlogs grew.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian cold climate utility operations review. Weather, flow and equipment records are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Overtime hours in the storm season doubled, concentrated in emergency callouts.
Planned inspection and cleaning fell to 60 percent of target during the same season.
Crew size was unchanged from the prior season, when overtime was half as high.
A standby roster with cross trained staff from other divisions was proposed before the season but not adopted.
Emergency response times stayed within standard despite the overtime load.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Crews were not working hard enough, which the doubled overtime contradicts
The season exposed a staffing structure gap, not a crew effort gap: emergency demand was met by overtime while planned work was sacrificed, exactly what a standby roster was proposed to prevent
Planned work should have been protected by refusing emergency callouts
Overtime is the proper way to staff storm seasons, so nothing should change

inference.explanation: Effort was maximal, response stayed in standard, and planned work still fell: the system absorbed the season by burning planned capacity. The unused standby proposal is the documented alternative.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Add permanent crew and keep the same season structure
Adopt the cross trained standby roster for the next storm season and protect planned work targets in the season plan
Ban overtime next season to force planned work completion

nextClue.explanation: Storm seasons are predictable enough to staff for, and overtime is a symptom, not a strategy.

clueText.nc-a: Permanent crew for a seasonal peak is the most expensive answer to a roster problem.
clueText.nc-b: The standby roster spreads emergency load so planned work survives the season.
clueText.nc-c: Banning overtime would leave emergencies unstaffed rather than staffed differently.

tasks.prompt: A Calgary CMOM annual review shows every activity target met, cleaning, inspection and repairs, while the outcome targets for blockages and overflows were missed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CMOM governance and performance review. Program records, targets and results are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Cleaning completed 102 percent of planned length and CCTV completed 100 percent of planned length.
Blockage rate rose from 6.1 to 7.4 per 100 km, against a target to fall below 5.
Overflow events rose slightly, with most traced to two basins cleaned late in the cycle.
The two problem basins were cleaned on schedule length but after their historic blockage season.
Crew records, equipment and materials were the same across basins.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The CMOM program is succeeding because all activity targets were met
Blockages rose because cleaning itself causes blockages
The program delivered its activities but mistimed them in the problem basins, so activity completion is masking an outcome failure
The blockage rate must be a counting error because cleaning was completed

inference.explanation: Full activity with rising blockages, concentrated where cleaning landed after the risk season, shows timing and outcome, not effort, are the gaps.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Re-sequence cleaning so high risk basins are cleaned before their blockage season, and report outcome rates as the headline CMOM result
Add 20 percent more cleaning length everywhere next year on the same schedule
Report activity completion as the headline and move outcome rates to an appendix

nextClue.explanation: CMOM governance judges a program by the failures it prevents, not the work it logs.

clueText.nc-a: The plan moves the two basins ahead of their season and leads the annual report with blockage and overflow rates.
clueText.nc-b: More length on the same late schedule repeats the timing failure at larger scale.
clueText.nc-c: Burying outcome rates is how a missed outcome stayed invisible this year.

tasks.prompt: An Edmonton CMOM audit finds corrective actions from the last three annual reviews still open, and checks what happened to each one.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CMOM governance and performance review. Program records, targets and results are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Nine of twelve corrective actions from three reviews are past their due dates.
None of the nine has a revised date, an owner update, or a closure record in the program file.
The same root cause, late cleaning in two basins, appears in findings in all three years.
Annual reviews recorded the actions as accepted each year without checking prior year status.
Budget and staffing for the actions were approved in each year they were raised.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The actions failed because their budgets were never approved
Corrective action tracking, not resources, is the governance failure: accepted actions were never followed up, so the same finding repeated for three years
Three different root causes explain the three yearly findings
The audit should close the nine actions now because they are old

inference.explanation: Funding was approved and the cause is identical each year. What is missing is any follow up record. Closing old actions on age alone would erase the lesson.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Raise the same actions a fourth year and trust the annual review to track them
Close all nine actions and start a fresh list with no history
Institute a corrective action register reviewed quarterly, with owner, due date and evidence of closure for every action

nextClue.explanation: A CMOM program without action follow up will rediscover the same failure every year.

clueText.nc-a: The annual review already failed to track them three times, so it cannot be the only check.
clueText.nc-b: Fresh lists with no history are how repeated findings stay invisible to governance.
clueText.nc-c: The register is reviewed quarterly and closure needs evidence, not just a date passing.

tasks.prompt: A Winnipeg CMOM performance report to council claims a 30 percent blockage reduction, and the utility manager verifies the claim before it is presented.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CMOM governance and performance review. Program records, targets and results are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: The 30 percent figure compares a partial current year, nine months, with a full prior year.
Full year to full year, the blockage rate per 100 km falls 8 percent.
The service area grew by annexation during the year, adding older pipe with higher blockage rates.
Raw blockage counts rose slightly, while the rate per 100 km fell because the network grew.
The counting method and blockage definition were unchanged across both years.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The honest verified result is an 8 percent rate reduction on a full year basis, and the 30 percent claim rests on a partial year comparison
The 30 percent claim is fair because partial years always run lower
Blockages actually rose, so no reduction of any kind can be reported
Annexation explains the entire rate change, so the program had no effect

inference.explanation: Same definitions, full year rates: an 8 percent fall is real but modest. The headline figure compares unlike periods, and raw counts ignore network growth.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Present the 30 percent figure and footnote the partial year in small print
Present the full year rate result with the annexation noted, and set a rule that council reports use complete periods and rates
Report raw counts only, since rates confuse council

nextClue.explanation: Governance reporting that needs a footnote to be honest is not honest reporting.

clueText.nc-a: A small print footnote does not cure a headline built on unlike periods.
clueText.nc-b: The council report leads with the full year rate, notes annexation, and adopts the complete period rule.
clueText.nc-c: Raw counts rose while service grew, so counts alone would misreport a real rate improvement.

tasks.prompt: A Regina utility reviews its CMOM capacity element after a wet year in which several trunks surcharged but no capacity study was triggered.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CMOM governance and performance review. Program records, targets and results are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: The CMOM plan requires a capacity study when any trunk surcharges in two storms in one year.
Level records show three trunks surcharged in three or more storms during the wet year.
No capacity study was started for any of the three trunks.
Operations staff logged the surcharge events correctly in the event system.
The plan assigns study triggering to a position left vacant for eight months of the year.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The plan itself is at fault because surcharge events were never recorded
Capacity studies were unnecessary because no overflow reached a watercourse
The trunks did not really surcharge because level sensors over read in wet weather
The capacity element failed at its trigger step: events were logged, but the vacant assigned role meant no study was started

inference.explanation: Logging worked and thresholds were clearly crossed. The single missing link is the unfilled role that owned the trigger, which is a governance gap, not a data gap.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Assign the trigger duty to a filled backup role and audit trigger compliance at each annual review
Lower the plan threshold so studies trigger more often next year
Remove the study trigger and rely on operator judgement alone

nextClue.explanation: A plan element that depends on one chair fails whenever that chair is empty.

clueText.nc-a: The duty gains a named backup and the annual review audits whether triggers fired.
clueText.nc-b: More triggers would still sit with a vacant role, so the failure would repeat.
clueText.nc-c: Removing the trigger discards a sound threshold because a staffing gap went unmanaged.

tasks.prompt: A Saskatoon CMOM review compares two districts with identical cleaning budgets and finds very different blockage outcomes.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CMOM governance and performance review. Program records, targets and results are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: District A targets cleaning by blockage history and root and grease findings, and its blockage rate falls 25 percent.
District B cleans on a fixed rotation by street order, and its blockage rate is unchanged.
Both districts spent the same budget, used the same crews and equipment pool, and cover similar pipe age.
District B cleaned more total length than District A during the review period.
Blockage counting and response practices are the same in both districts.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Fixed rotation is fairer and therefore better, regardless of blockage outcomes
District A improved because it cleaned more length than District B
Targeting cleaning by risk evidence outperformed fixed rotation at equal cost, so the CMOM cleaning element should be risk based
District B crews must be less skilled, which the shared crew pool contradicts

inference.explanation: Equal budgets, shared crews, more length in B, yet only the risk targeted district improved. Method of selection, not effort or spend, explains the split.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Extend fixed rotation to District A so both districts are treated identically
Give District B a larger budget to compensate for its unchanged rate
Convert the cleaning element to risk based selection citywide, keeping rotation only as a maximum interval backstop

nextClue.explanation: Equal treatment of unlike risk is not fairness in a maintenance program, it is waste.

clueText.nc-a: Identical treatment produced the worse result in B and would import it to A.
clueText.nc-b: More budget for the same selection method buys more of what did not work.
clueText.nc-c: Risk based selection is adopted citywide with a backstop interval so no pipe goes uncleaned indefinitely.

tasks.prompt: A Kelowna CMOM self assessment scores the utility high on every element, and an external peer review of the same program reaches different scores.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CMOM governance and performance review. Program records, targets and results are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: The self assessment used activity records, such as kilometres cleaned, as evidence for every element.
The peer review asked for outcome evidence, such as overflow trends and repeat blockage rates, for the same elements.
On outcome evidence, two elements score low: overflow response learning and capacity assurance.
Overflow events and repeat blockages are flat over the self assessment period.
Both reviews examined the same program documents and the same period.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The peer review must be wrong because it used the same documents
The self assessment overstated program maturity by scoring activities instead of outcomes, and the peer outcome based scores are the credible ones
The utility should score itself higher next year to offset the peer scores
Flat overflow trends prove the program needs no improvement

inference.explanation: Same documents, different evidence standard. Flat outcomes cannot support high maturity scores, whichever review is kinder.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Keep activity based scoring and note the peer review as an outlier
Rebuild the self assessment to require outcome evidence for every element score
Stop external peer reviews so scores stay consistent

nextClue.explanation: Self assessment that grades effort instead of results will always report a program better than it is.

clueText.nc-a: Calling the outcome based review an outlier protects the weaker method, not the program.
clueText.nc-b: Each element score must now cite an outcome measure, with activity records as supporting detail only.
clueText.nc-c: Ending peer review removes the only check that caught the scoring gap.

tasks.prompt: A Red Deer utility sets CMOM targets for the next cycle and must choose between targets based on its own trend and targets copied from a top performing peer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CMOM governance and performance review. Program records, targets and results are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: The utility blockage rate is 7.2 per 100 km and has fallen about 5 percent per year for three years.
The peer rate of 2.0 per 100 km comes from a system with mostly newer pipe and combined sewer separation completed.
The utility own pipe stock is older, and its separation program is only one third complete.
A target copied from the peer would require a 70 percent cut in one cycle.
The utility three year trend, if held, reaches about 6.1 per 100 km next cycle.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A credible target extends the utility own verified trend toward the peer direction, rather than copying a peer rate its asset stock cannot yet support
Copy the peer target of 2.0, because ambitious targets always improve performance
Set no target, because peer comparison is meaningless between different systems
Set the target at 7.2 unchanged, because the trend might not hold

inference.explanation: Peer context explains the gap: asset age and separation status differ. A 70 percent one cycle cut is not a target, it is a fiction, while the trend based figure is demanding and reachable.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Adopt a trend based target near 6.1 per 100 km with the peer gap and its asset reasons reported alongside
Adopt 2.0 per 100 km as the cycle target and report progress against it
Drop benchmarking from the CMOM report entirely

nextClue.explanation: Targets govern behaviour: an impossible target teaches staff to game or ignore the numbers.

clueText.nc-a: The cycle target follows the verified trend and the report explains the peer gap by asset age and separation status.
clueText.nc-b: Reporting against 2.0 would show failure even in a year of real improvement.
clueText.nc-c: Benchmarking still shows direction and gap; it just cannot set the number directly.

tasks.prompt: A Brandon CMOM annual review must decide whether a rise in customer backup reports means the maintenance program is failing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CMOM governance and performance review. Program records, targets and results are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Backup reports rise 20 percent in the year a new online reporting portal launches.
Field verified backups, confirmed by crew inspection, are unchanged from the prior year.
The portal added reports from addresses that previously phoned a number with limited hours.
Repeat verified backups at the same addresses fall during the year.
Sewer blockage findings on inspection are unchanged year over year.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The maintenance program is failing because customer reports rose 20 percent
The portal should be closed so report counts return to the old level
Verified backups must be undercounted because reports rose
The report rise reflects easier reporting through the new portal, while verified backups and repeat events, the program outcome measures, are stable or improving

inference.explanation: The channel changed, not the sewers. Verified events flat, repeats down, findings flat: the outcome record does not support a failing program verdict.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Judge the program on raw report counts as before
Discount all portal reports as unreliable
Report verified and repeat backup rates as the CMOM outcome measures, with raw report counts shown as demand data

nextClue.explanation: Counting reports instead of verified events punishes a utility for making reporting easier.

clueText.nc-a: Raw counts already produced the false failure signal this review corrects.
clueText.nc-b: Portal reports led to verified inspections; discarding them would lose real demand information.
clueText.nc-c: The annual review adopts verified and repeat rates as outcomes and keeps raw counts as service demand context.

tasks.prompt: A Prince George CMOM review examines the legal and regulatory reporting element after a late overflow report is filed with the province.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian CMOM governance and performance review. Program records, targets and results are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: The overflow was detected, contained and cleaned up within the utility response standard.
The written report to the province was filed nine days after the event, past the utility internal reporting target.
The delay came from the report waiting on one manager approval while that manager was on leave.
No backup approver is named in the reporting procedure.
All event facts needed for the report were recorded on the day of the event.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Crews responded too slowly, which the response record contradicts
The facts were not available in time to file the report
Field response met the standard and the failure is a single approver bottleneck in the reporting procedure, a governance design flaw
The internal target should be extended to ten days so the filing counts as on time

inference.explanation: Facts were complete on day one and response was timely. Only approval stalled, behind one absent person with no named backup. Moving the target would hide, not fix, that.

nextClue.prompt: Which step best follows from this finding?

options.label: Discipline the crew that handled the overflow response
Name backup approvers in the reporting procedure and track filing timeliness as a CMOM measure
Extend the internal reporting target to cover approval delays

nextClue.explanation: Procedures that route critical filings through one person fail on the first vacation.

clueText.nc-a: The crew met the response standard, so discipline would punish the wrong link in the chain.
clueText.nc-b: Backup approvers are named and filing timeliness joins the CMOM measures reviewed each cycle.
clueText.nc-c: Extending the target makes late filings look compliant without filing any sooner.
